OpenZIM - For making websites browsable offline

"The openZIM project proposes offline storage solutions for content coming from the Web. The project has two different targets:

Definition of the ZIM file format: an open and standardized file format,
Implementation of the zimlib: an open source (GPLv2) implementation of the ZIM file format."
I don't understand the point. HTML files and wget already exist and seem to cover the same ground.

Let us take an example like Wikipedia. You might want to have it all available in a browsable way when you are on your desert island. By taking a snapshot of Wikipedia in a zim format, you can later view that offline using Kiwix. That is possible right now!

What we could theoretically do with this is, for example, archive Voat as it currently exists, today, with all its threads and comments. You could have that to read on your desert island, too.

You can do that with the HTML, CSS, and JS files and your normal browser. Just make an offline mirror with wget.

There's no real need to jam it all into an alternative file format AFAICT. This seems like an example of how people like to reimplement things that already exist and you end up with n+1 competing formats.

Scraping is impractical with Wikipedia. And the dumps of such large sites aren't provided in convenient databases indexed for local consumption -- even though they should be. So programs like Kiwix use a specialized database format derived from a legacy format, which works pretty well for its purpose, and saves untold local processing power by distributing dumps in their own favored format from Wikipedia, Wiktionary, etc.

Maybe one day the Wikimedia Foundation will release data in an end-user consumable format and obsolete all this arcanery.
